title: Segregation of Plasmids in Bacterial Colonies
author: Tamara Matute
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jbncime

steps.title: Co-transform and plate E. coli
steps.instruction: Co-transform E. coli bacteria with two segregating plasmids (e.g., SEG10 and SEG11) and plate them on LB agar plates supplemented with arabinose and the antibiotics specific for each plasmid (e.g., carbenicillin and tetracycline).

substeps.instruction: Use concentrations: Arabinose 10 mM, Chloramphenicol 10 µg/ml, Carbenicillin 100 µg/ml, and Tetracycline 10 µg/ml.

steps.title: Incubate plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at 37°C overnight, avoiding long periods of growth to prevent reducing the number of bacteria carrying both plasmids.

steps.title: Screen for co-transformed colonies
steps.instruction: Check colonies using fluorescence imaging; homogenous expression of both fluorescent proteins indicates co-transformed colonies.

steps.title: Liquid culture expansion
steps.instruction: Pick a co-transformed colony and incubate the cells in liquid LB media supplemented with arabinose and the same specific antibiotics used in the first step (e.g., carbenicillin and tetracycline).

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 5 hours at 37°C with shaking at 250 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest cells
steps.instruction: Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 3000 rpm for 10 minutes and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Re-suspend cells
steps.instruction: Re-suspend the cells in 5 ml of fresh LB media supplemented with the antibiotic common to both SEG plasmids (e.g., chloramphenicol for SEG10 and SEG11).

steps.title: Dilute culture
steps.instruction: Dilute the culture 1:5000 using fresh LB media supplemented with the antibiotic common to both SEG plasmids (e.g., chloramphenicol for SEG10 and SEG11).

steps.title: Plate diluted cells
steps.instruction: Spread 10 µl of the dilution onto LB agar plates supplemented with the common antibiotic for both SEG plasmids (e.g., chloramphenicol for SEG10 and SEG11).

substeps.instruction: Note: 10 µl typically produces ~50 colonies per plate; adjust dilution or volume as needed based on metabolic burden.

steps.title: Incubate for colony growth
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates at 37°C for 8-12 hours until colonies are visible.

steps.title: Additional liquid growth
steps.instruction: Grow cells in liquid culture for an additional 3 hours.
